scope: Evidence, cue-selection, provenance, operationalisation and schema contract for a future headline access gate; no executable mechanism or user interface.

selected.label: Headline negativity
basis: Registered Report with large same-story headline field experiments and a clear directional access target.
Public Upworthy archive supports open provenance and independent reanalysis of the source data.
Archive maintainers report that the negativity result remained nearly identical after excluding tests affected by the 2024 randomization-integrity concern.
A binary controlled cue is sufficient for the first model-discrimination experiment and avoids false precision.
limitations: Primary causal evidence is concentrated in Upworthy 2013-2015 and must not be generalized as a universal negativity effect.
Recent preliminary experimental work reports no expected negativity-bias effect in a different two-stage design.
Published sentiment operationalisations use restricted or non-redistributable lexical resources, so runtime scoring must not depend on them.

deferred.label: Headline simplicity
basis: Field experiments from The Washington Post and Upworthy support greater selection of simpler headlines.
A preregistered follow-up signal-detection study supports a distinct later recognition/processing effect.
limitations: The published simplicity index is composite and includes LIWC-derived components.
Washington Post Study Set 1 data are restricted by a data-use agreement.
Some component behavior differs across publisher datasets, requiring an additional operationalisation audit before executable use.

sources.citation: Robertson, C. E., Pröllochs, N., Schwarzenegger, K., Pärnamets, P., Van Bavel, J. J., & Feuerriegel, S. (2023). Negativity drives online news consumption. Nature Human Behaviour, 7, 812-822.
sources.data_license_note: Underlying Upworthy Research Archive is CC BY 4.0; no source lexicon is redistributed by CBD.
sources.notes: Registered Report. Directional target is higher negative-language content associated with greater click propensity within same-story headline experiments. Published magnitudes are context only.

sources.citation: Matias, J. N., Munger, K., Le Quere, M. A., & Ebersole, C. (2021). The Upworthy Research Archive, a time series of 32,487 experiments in U.S. media. Scientific Data, 8, 195.
sources.data_license_note: Archive data are available under CC BY 4.0.
sources.notes: Documents experiment-arm assignment, impressions, clicks, headline/image package structure and open archive provenance.

sources.citation: Matias, J. N., Munger, K., Le Quere, M. A., & Ebersole, C. (2024). Author Correction: The Upworthy Research Archive, a time series of 32,487 experiments in U.S. media. Scientific Data, 11, 765.
sources.data_license_note: Correction to the open archive documentation.
sources.notes: Reports likely randomization problems between 25 June 2013 and 10 January 2014. Must accompany any causal use of the archive.

sources.citation: Gligorić, K., Lifchits, G., West, R., & Anderson, A. (2023). Linguistic effects on news headline success: Evidence from thousands of online field experiments. PLOS ONE, 18(3), e0281682.
sources.data_license_note: Uses the same public Upworthy archive and is not an independent replication population.
sources.notes: Convergent registered analysis of linguistic features within the same Upworthy archive; same-dataset evidence must not be double-counted as independent replication.

sources.citation: Qiu, J., & Golman, R. (2024). Curiosity in news consumption. Applied Cognitive Psychology, 38(2), e4195.
sources.data_license_note: Article is open access; source-platform data access is not a CBD runtime dependency.
sources.notes: More than 100,000 WeChat articles show lower headline valence predicts more reads after controls. Predictive observational support, not randomized causal replication.

sources.citation: Shulman, H. C., Markowitz, D. M., & Rogers, T. (2024). Reading dies in complexity: Online news consumers prefer simple writing. Science Advances, 10(23), eadn2555. Washington Post field-experiment evidence unit.
sources.data_license_note: Study Set 1 data cannot be publicly released under the authors' data-use agreement with The Washington Post.
sources.notes: Independent traditional-newsroom headline experiments supporting greater CTR for simpler headlines; source data are restricted.

sources.citation: Shulman, H. C., Markowitz, D. M., & Rogers, T. (2024). Reading dies in complexity: Online news consumers prefer simple writing. Science Advances, 10(23), eadn2555. Upworthy evidence unit.
sources.data_license_note: Uses the public Upworthy archive and shares its population with other Upworthy analyses.
sources.notes: Convergent Upworthy evidence for the deferred simplicity cue; not independent of Robertson/Gligoric at the archive-population level.

sources.citation: Shulman, H. C., Markowitz, D. M., & Rogers, T. (2024). Reading dies in complexity: Online news consumers prefer simple writing. Science Advances, 10(23), eadn2555. Preregistered signal-detection evidence unit.
sources.data_license_note: Studies 2-4 data/code/materials are reported as available through OSF/Harvard Dataverse.
sources.notes: Follow-up experiment separates headline selection from later recognition/sensitivity; relevant to a future attention/encoding stage, not Paccess calibration.

sources.citation: Nickl, P. L., Hills, T., & Lorenz-Spreen, P. (2025). The effects of an experimental attention economy on the production and consumption of news headlines. PsyArXiv preprint.
sources.data_license_note: Preprint-level evidence; conference presentation is the same project, not a second study.
sources.notes: Two-stage producer/consumer experiment. APS 2026 abstract reports no expected negativity-bias effect; preprint reports more informative headlines were more likely to be clicked.

sources.citation: Mattis, N., & Heitz, L. (2025). Nudges for news recommenders: prominent article positioning increases selection, engagement, and recall of environmental news, but reducing complexity does not. Journal of Communication, 75(6), 437-450.
sources.data_license_note: Article and linked research infrastructure/dataset are publicly described; intervention concerns article-text complexity rather than a headline-only simplicity manipulation.
sources.notes: Preregistered seven-day UK field experiment. Reduced article-text complexity did not significantly affect selection, reading time or recall; not a direct replication of headline simplicity.

planned_quantities.definition: Controlled headline-negativity condition reserved for the future M1.E3 reference comparator.
planned_quantities.what_it_is_not: Not truth, factuality, misinformation, article valence, experienced emotion, political orientation or source quality.

planned_quantities.definition: Future latent probability of opening/clicking a full item after one registered preview impression.
planned_quantities.what_it_is_not: Not observed population CTR, attention, reading time, comprehension, belief, Pengage or Share.

planned_quantities.definition: Future reference binary outcome indicating open/click versus no open/click.
planned_quantities.what_it_is_not: Not attention, reading completion, endorsement, belief or sharing.

planned_quantities.definition: Future registered event that a preview/headline was rendered under the M1.E3 reference task.
planned_quantities.what_it_is_not: Not proof of fixation, reading, encoding, recall or full-content access.

empirical_target.comparison: higher versus lower registered headline-negativity cue within otherwise comparable same-story headline conditions

design.count_note: Confirmatory filtered analysis reported 12,448 RCTs, 53,699 headline variants, over 205 million impressions and 2,778,124 clicks; broader archive context is larger.

effect_context.scale_note: Published standardized coefficient for the proportion of negative words; 99% confidence interval.
Approximate reported CTR increase per additional negative word for a headline of average length; context-specific transformation.

empirical_target.model_match: The future M1.E3 candidate may use only the directional higher-Hneg to higher-Paccess target. Published magnitudes do not set the future reference coefficient.
empirical_target.limitations: Historical Upworthy context, headline-feature operationalisation and platform-specific selection environment limit generalization. Archive correction and robust reliable-test reanalysis must remain attached to provenance.

planned_patterns.name: Headline-negativity access differential
planned_patterns.pattern: Higher registered Hneg must correspond to higher future Paccess in the selected controlled M1.E3 reference comparator.

planned_patterns.name: Access-gate null
planned_patterns.pattern: When the selected headline cue is normalized or disabled, otherwise identical future M1.E3 conditions must converge in Paccess.

planned_patterns.name: Access is not downstream cognition
planned_patterns.pattern: Changing the future M1.E3 access cue must not directly mutate retained M0 belief or Share, M1.E1 Aissue, or M1.E2 Pengage and EngageIntent.

planned_patterns.name: Non-click preserves headline exposure
planned_patterns.pattern: A future Access value of zero must not erase the registered PreviewImpression event or imply that the headline preview was never rendered.

operationalization.divergence_from_source: CBD freezes a binary controlled condition for model discrimination rather than reproducing the source paper's continuous LIWC negative-word proportion or its reported effect-size scale.
restricted_resources_not_redistributed: Washington Post Study Set 1 headline data
